# SAMPLE RUNS — MSME (Chinese SME enterprise credit)

**Committee-facing acceptance pack (reviewed BEFORE the Go/No-Go decision).** Generated by `ml_models/score_acceptance_cases.py` from `msme.json` — reproducible, not one-off.

**Model:** AEGIS-approved WOE-logistic (15 features) · **Portfolio default rate:** 6.0% · PD floored at 0.03% (Basel CRE32.3).

> **Scope.** This pack reports only methodology/regulation-grounded outputs: calibrated PD, rating grade (risk tier, on the institution's internal master scale), exact WOE reason codes, and the governed completeness decision. The **accept / refer / decline lending decision is set by the institution applying its own risk-appetite PD threshold** — it is exogenous to this methodology and is **not** derived or priced here.

**Case composition (fixed standard):** 4 real applicants (drawn from the dataset, observed outcome shown — defaulted / repaid) + 2 synthetic composites (constructed from observed feature-value extremes; outcome shown is the construction intent, "(by design)", not an observed outcome — a PD-floor check and a stress check). Real cases span the risk range and include both outcomes.

> **⚠️ EPV note on the synthetic stress case.** `SYN-worst` (each feature at its worst *observed* value, by correlation sign) scores **0.03% AAA — the same as `SYN-best`**, not a high risk. This is **not a bug**: at EPV ≈ 1.2 the per-feature risk directions are so weak and non-monotonic that their extremes do not compose into a coherent high-risk firm — the model has **no stable "worst case" to construct**. `SYN-best` still serves as the PD-floor check. The failed stress case is itself an EPV finding, reinforcing MoC-epv (treat PDs as indicative, not precise).
